correctness.rationale: Exact active-set KKT Jacobians and step-vector basis reduce the global nonlinear modulus to a finite selector maximum. A binary transition lemma yields the exact count. The integer deficit identity proves nonnegativity in all dimensions and the unique 1/(n+1) exceptional residue gap. Four explicit selector families and strict KKT perturbations attain the bounds. The actual packaged checker was replayed: 36,813 exact active-set tests through dimension 11, 109 exact integer-optimization checks through dimension 120, 1,500 nonlinear rational pairs. Finite tests are not used for the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The original scientific gap is quantitative two-input stability of a standard nonlinear probability-calibration operator under ordered-data variation. The all-dimensional closed formula has sharp linear growth, an exceptional residue class, attained finite pairs and a first expansive dimension different from the previously solved cycle case. This distinguishes open-boundary error amplification in a practically natural setting and gives reproducible benchmark constants beyond ordinary Hilbert nonexpansivity.
